results.summary:
hkb doctor now surfaces KB_TOKEN's expiry. GitHub sends `github-authentication-token-expiration` on every response to a fine-grained PAT; doctor reads it off the `GET rate_limit` response it was already making (switched that one call to restRaw — no new API call, and rate_limit is not charged). Above 7 days it is a green line with the date; under 7 days a warning naming the fix (mint a new PAT, gh secret set KB_TOKEN); past the date the check fails so doctor exits 1. OAuth/classic tokens send no header and get no line; an unparseable header is treated as no header. In Actions the finding is also emitted as ::warning::/::error:: (stderr under --json so stdout stays one JSON document; %/CR/LF escaped). New exports in src/doctor.js: tokenExpiry, expiryFinding, checkTokenExpiry, checkToken, actionsAnnotation, emitAnnotations, tokenExpiryNotice.

NOT DONE, deliberately: the loop's call site. tokenExpiryNotice(ctx, log) implements the once-a-day check (throttled by a token_expiry_day stamp in .kanban/state.json; a failed probe stamps nothing so the next tick retries), but wiring it needs one line in src/dispatch.js — outside this task's declared scope, and #36 was editing that file concurrently. Whoever owns dispatch.js next should add `await tokenExpiryNotice(ctx, log);` at the top of the loop body, before tick(). Note the annotation there bypasses `log` on purpose: the loop timestamps every line and the runner only reads a workflow command that starts the line.
